name: lnk_parse
description: Parse a Windows shell link (.lnk), or every link structure found in a slice of a dump, by the MS-SHLLINK layout. Decoded: the flags; the three FILETIMEs (raw decimal and ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits, integer arithmetic); LinkInfo (VolumeID: drive type, serial number as eight hex digits, label; local base path and common path suffix, ANSI and Unicode; CommonNetworkRelativeLink: share, device name, provider type); the string data; the extra blocks it recognises; `linkinfo_target` joins them as the specification defines. Heuristic, not a decode: `idlist_ascii`, `idlist_paths` and `utf16_strings` are printable runs searched for in the bytes, not the shell item list. ANSI strings are in a code page the file does not record and are shown as Latin-1. A read that ends inside the structure says so under `problems` and `structure_complete`. A scan carves by the 20-byte header signature: a hit is a candidate. It executes nothing and resolves no target. SENSITIVE: a link's arguments and strings can hold a command line with a secret in it; run it as a job with secret_output: true when they may.

size.description: Bytes to read (default 4096, at most 268435456); structure_complete and problems say whether the link ended inside them

scan.description: Scan the slice for multiple LNK headers

each.description: Bytes per LNK when scanning (default: up to the next LNK header, or the end of what was read)

max.description: LNKs shown inline when scanning (default 50, an inline page size); every one found is kept, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results
